extracted.intended_audience: Referees/reviewers for Econometrica and other Econometric Society journals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing a referee report for Econometrica: timeliness, tone, required structure (Summary, Essential Points, Suggestions), length, and policies (including AI use).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit your referee report within six weeks, or by another comparably prompt date you propose when accepting the assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We aim to improve the speed and quality of the editorial process. If you are unable to meet this timeline, promptly decline the invitation. Timely reports are essential to editorial efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify handling Co-Editor if previously refereed
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have previously refereed the manuscript, inform the handling Co-Editor immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps editors avoid duplicate effort and provides context about prior evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional Tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Referee reports should be constructive, respectful, and focused on the scholarly content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the confidential letter to the Co-Editor may include candid assessments, the report shared with the authors should avoid gratuitous or dismissive remarks. Unnecessarily harsh comments undermine the profession and are discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential comments to Co-Editor may be candid
rubrics_metrics.description: The confidential letter to the Co-Editor may include candid assessments not suitable for the author-facing report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the confidential channel for frank advice to the editor, but ensure the public report remains professional and constructive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure — Summary section
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a brief summary of the paper as you understand it, emphasizing the key contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear summary helps the Co-Editor assess how you interpret the paper and ensures shared understanding. If parts of the paper are unclear, noting this can illuminate possible communication issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure — Essential Points section
rubrics_metrics.description: List the critical issues the authors must address for the paper to meet Econometrica's publication standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be as precise as possible about what is required. This list should normally contain no more than three essential points; if substantially more are needed, a rejection is typically more appropriate. If recommending rejection, use this section to identify the central problems. Also comment—where relevant—on whether the paper could be made more concise and which results are essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure — Suggestions section
rubrics_metrics.description: Include helpful recommendations that are not essential to address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are discretionary suggestions (conceptual, organizational, or stylistic) that can improve the work. The authors retain discretion over development. The guidelines expect approximately 70% of the content in a traditional referee report will naturally fall into this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length and scope of reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Referee reports need not be long; for most papers two to three pages are sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional comments in the Suggestions section are welcome but should not delay timely submission of the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concision and identifying nonessential material
rubrics_metrics.description: Comment where relevant on whether the paper could be made more concise and which results or proofs are essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask which results could be cut or have proofs shortened. Identifying nonessential material can help authors focus the paper and meet journal standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid requests for nonessential extensions or additional appendices
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for nonessential extensions or for additional appendices (especially supplemental online material) should generally be avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such requests may unnecessarily inflate the paper; focus on what is essential for publication rather than optional expansions.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI policy for referees
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees are expected to read the submission themselves and form their own independent evaluation of the work; AI tools may be used only to help shape and communicate views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI can be used to improve clarity of suggestions, organize comments, or polish report language. In all cases the report must reflect the referee’s own judgment and evaluation of the manuscript.
